liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Spanish Jam** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out Spanish Jam as essential listening from this show; Spanish Jam is called wonderful, possibly the best of its era [3][8][10][12]
- **Clementine** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Clementine among the Dead's best, behind only the 26 January 1969 version, citing its jazzy swing; Clementine is rated as A+, leading into New Potato Caboose and Born Cross Eyed [6][17]
- **New Potato Caboose** (1 review): Psychedelic New Potato Caboose into Born Cross Eyed is described as vintage and the reviewer's main reason for listening [11]
- **Born Cross Eyed** (1 review): The band slams into Born Cross Eyed relentlessly [13]
- **Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)** (1 review): Caution is very short and ends explosively, seeming to build toward something more [7]
- **Dark Star** (1 other source): Dark Star on this tape consists of only its first several notes [3]
- **Caution Jam** (1 review): Short Caution jam drives along powerfully but fizzles out too early; reviewer wishes it had continued [10]

## The recordings

- **gd68-01-20.sbd.jools.19470.sbe-fixed.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 33 min; rated 4.72/5 by 43 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape sounds clear for its age, though the recording cuts off during Dark Star; Recording quality is quite good for its age, but vocals are minimal; Described as a crisp soundboard recording, though only a short portion of the show exists [7][12][17]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.miller.97340.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 33 min; rated 4.44/5 by 32 [2]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.ward.47.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 31 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [3]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.abe.4990.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 31 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [4]

## Around the show

- Show is incomplete, but the band sounds especially deepened and fully like the Grateful Dead that night [13]
- DeadBase lists a jam before Clementine; the tape reportedly starts on an announcer's remark about cranking it up [1]
- Only about 35 minutes of this show circulated [23]
- Reviewer says Phil plays a Clementine part during the long Other One jam on 4/26/72, around 15-20 minutes in [10]
- Clementine here is judged much better than the 2/2/68 version on the So Many Roads box set [11]
- Born Cross Eyed, Caboose and Spanish Jam all appear on Anthem of the Sun but were dropped early in 1968 [14]
- Reviewer understands dropping Born Cross Eyed as too hard to play, but wishes New Potato Caboose had survived [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-01-20.sbd.jools.19470.sbe-fixed.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer's older copy lacked the short Dark Star at the end; this version is more complete; Uploader's DAT copy cuts Dark Star early; a cassette copy runs a minute or two longer before cutting off [1][14]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.miller.97340.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: Transferred from a DAT from Rob Eaton, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.ward.47.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> MReel -> DAT -> CD-R [3]. Also: Not an FM recording; broadcast on Grateful Dead Hour 342 [3]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.abe.4990.sbeok.shnf**: source: CD > EAC > SHN [4]

## Art and photos

- Photo by Zoooma (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead poster for 1/20/68 Municipal Auditorium, Eureka, California](https://www.flickr.com/photos/9692677@N07/2925190826/) [25]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/9692677@N07/2925190826/) [26]
